key_insight: A semantics-first latent representation can improve 3D MRI reconstruction and cross-contrast synthesis by preserving anatomical coherence and clinically meaningful detail before generation.
engineering_relevance: This work offers a more scalable latent-space pipeline for multi-contrast MRI, helping reduce compute while improving image quality for downstream medical imaging systems.
method: Latent Harmonization Encoder (LHE) captures long-range volumetric anatomy in the compressed representation.
Semantic Recovery Block (SRB) restores high-level contrast-aware semantics using a self-supervised semantic teacher.
Anatomy-aware Frequency Loss (AFL) preserves diagnostically important high-frequency structures and reduces over-smoothing.
evidence_signal: Experiments on two public multi-contrast MRI datasets show consistent gains in both reconstruction fidelity and cross-contrast synthesis quality.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of latent compression and semantic supervision, so the added modules may increase training complexity and require careful tuning.
paper_title: Recover Semantics First, Generate Better: Improved Latent Modeling for 3D MRI Reconstruction and Cross-Contrast Synthesis
